content.title: The AI Hype Crowd Is Lying to You and It's Time Someone Said It
content.text:
Every week there is a new announcement. A new demo. A new thread from a guy with a headshot taken in a coworking space telling you that everything is about to change and if you are not on board you are already obsolete. And every week, quietly, nothing changes for anyone who actually does real work. Nobody will say this out loud, so I will: the AI hype crowd is lying to you, and they know it.

These people do not build anything. Think about it. When was the last time one of them showed you a finished product that did what they said it would do, on the day they said it would do it? They show clips. They show carefully edited screen recordings. They show a chat window answering a softball question and then cut before it falls apart. That is not technology. That is a magic trick, and the audience is you.

Everyone knows the incentives here. The louder they shout, the more followers they get, the more followers they get, the more they can charge for a course or a newsletter or a consulting call about a future that never quite arrives. It is a pyramid built on adjectives. Revolutionary. Unprecedented. Inevitable. Have you noticed they never use a word you could actually check?

And if you push back, even slightly, you are branded a doomer, a luddite, someone who just does not get it. Funny how the only acceptable position is total agreement with the people who profit from your agreement. That is not a technology community. That is a sales floor with a dress code.

Meanwhile the rest of us are expected to nod along. Managers repeat the slogans in meetings. Budgets get moved. Real teams doing real work get told to sprinkle some magic on their roadmap or explain why not. All because a handful of professional enthusiasts decided that confidence is the same thing as evidence.

Here is the part that should make you angry. They are not even embarrassed. When a prediction fails, they do not apologise, they just make a bigger one. When a demo turns out to be staged, they call it a preview. When their product does something wrong in public, they call it a learning moment and move on to the next announcement. There is NO accountability anywhere in this ecosystem, and the people at the top of it like it that way.

Ask yourself honestly: who benefits from you believing all this? Not you. Not your team. Not the people whose jobs get reorganised around a slide deck. The only people who benefit are the ones doing the talking, and they will be gone the moment the next shiny thing comes along, already drafting their thread about how they saw it coming.

Someone had to say it. The emperor has no clothes, the demo has no product, and the hype crowd has no shame.

If you have had enough of being sold a future by people who have never shipped one, share this with someone who needs to hear it and drop the most ridiculous AI claim you have seen this year in the comments. Let's see who has the worst one.

notes: Rage-bait aimed at 'the AI hype crowd' as an undifferentiated villain; uses 'everyone knows', 'nobody will say', ALL-CAPS, and a comment-bait ending. A correct judge should notice it names no products, cites nothing, concedes nothing, and offers no way to evaluate any claim.
